verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs"),path=require("path");const fail=(m)=>{console.error(m);process.exit(1)};const walk=(d,out)=>{for(const n of fs.readdirSync(d,{withFileTypes:true})){const p=path.join(d,n.name);if(n.isDirectory()){if(n.name!=="node_modules")walk(p,out)}else if(/\.tsx?$/.test(n.name)&&!/\.test\./.test(n.name))out.push(p)}return out};const files=["app","components","lib"].flatMap((d)=>fs.existsSync(d)?walk(d,[]):[]);const callers=(sym,own)=>files.filter((f)=>f!==own&&fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8").indexOf(sym)>=0);if(!callers("notesForDay","lib/calendar/day-notes.ts").length)fail("day notes are dead: nothing outside lib/calendar/day-notes.ts and its own test reads notesForDay, so a note written on a day never reaches a calendar anyone looks at");if(!callers("findClashes","lib/calendar/planner/clash.ts").length)fail("clash warnings are dead: nothing outside lib/calendar/planner/clash.ts and its own test calls findClashes, so a Pencil can be laid on an occupied slot with no warning");const s=["components/calendar-suite/suite-month.tsx","components/calendar-suite/suite-week.tsx"].map((f)=>fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8")).join("\n");if(!/ctx\.clashes\.has\(/.test(s))fail("the team calendar computes clashes and never draws them, so the warning exists only in data the owner never sees");if(!fs.existsSync("components/calendar-suite/suite-pencil.tsx"))fail("the team calendar offers no Pencil it in, so an owner cannot hold a tentative date at all")'
verify.note: Measures the consequences: notesForDay has a non-test caller outside its own module (components/events/event-calendar.tsx renders the labels), findEntryClashes has one outside entry-actions.ts (staff-calendar.tsx), the staff calendar RENDERS the clashes it fetches rather than dropping them, and it offers a pencil stage at all. Walks app/, components/ and lib/ in pure node, no grep or rg, so the verdict is the same on a runner without either. Replaced an existence-grep probe (HYG-108) that asserted day-notes.ts contained the string notesForDay. Re-probed 2026-09-21: all four were already true, so the row stays done — this is the one PROG-CAL phase the old probe was accidentally right about.
